title: Spaghetti & Meatballs
description:
Spaghetti & Meatballs is probably the ultimate comfort food -- and with good reason – it’s comforting and always feels like home!
Made well, the meatballs are a tasty and succulent pleasure. And, a good freshly made sauce is a treat that doesn’t require all that much work.
All of this, with some good bread (maybe garlic bread), a simple oil and vinegar-dressed salad, and, of course, family or friends, and you’re in heaven on earth!
START TO FINISH: 1 ½ HOURS
Spaghetti & Meatballs
Start with the sauce. If you’re using whole tomatoes, put them in a large bowl and crush them with you hands.
In a big pot, heat the oil on medium heat, and sauté the onion for 5 minutes or so. Add the garlic and sauté until lightly golden brown, about 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and salt. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Stir in the basil, pepper, and oregano.
While the sauce is simmering, preheat the oven to 425 degrees and make the meatballs.
Let the breadcrumbs or stale bread pieces soak in the milk or water for a few moments.
Break up the meat into a large bowl or make a mound with a hole in the center on your cutting board or work surface. Sprinkle all around the salt, pepper, minced onion and garlic, eggs, grated cheese, parsley, and the bread crumbs with the liquid squeezed out.
Mix gently with your hands until every-thing is nicely distributed, but don’t over mix.
With a little olive oil on your hands, shape into 12 or so meatballs by gently scooping up a handful of meat and rolling it into a nice even ball, about 2 inches in diameter.
Put the meatballs in an oiled roasting pan, with the smashed garlic clove (for smell), and bake for 25 minutes, turning when a little browned, about half way through cooking (they’ll cook more in the sauce).
Prepare large pot of boiling salted water for the spaghetti.
By this point the marinara sauce will have finished its initial simmer. Add the roasted meatballs to the sauce and simmer together for another 30 minutes, stirring very gently occasionally.
During the last simmering together, cook the spaghetti until al dente.
When it’s done, drain it and return it to the pot it was cooked in. Add the chopped fresh basil and a couple of ladles of sauce.
Put the pot over medium high heat and, with wooden spoons or tongs, gently toss the pasta with the sauce until well coated, about 1 minute.
Transfer to a warmed platter and ladle more sauce over the spaghetti, together with the meatballs. Sprinkle with some grated cheese.
Bring some extra sauce and cheese for the table.

Marinara Sauce 
 3 28-ounce can Italian plum
 tomatoes
 ½ cup olive oil
 1 medium onion, minced
 6 garlic cloves, lightly smashed
 1 tablespoon plus 2 teaspoons
 kosher salt
 ¼ cup chopped fresh basic
 1 teaspoon ground pepper
 ¼ teaspoon dried oregano

 Meatballs
 ½ pound ground beef
 ½ pound ground pork
 ½ pound ground veal
 1 tablespoon salt
 ½ teaspoon ground pepper
 1 onion, minced
 1 garlic clove, minced
 1 garlic clove, lightly smashed
 2 eggs, lightly beaten
 1 cup grated cheese, mixture
 of Parmesan Reggiano
 and Locatelli Romano
 1 cup breadcrumbs, or stale
 bread, broken into little
 pieces
 1½ cups milk or water
 1 tablespoon chopped fresh
 parsley
 1 cup olive oil, or more

 1 pound dried spaghetti
 (Ronzoni wins taste tests)
 ¼ cup chopped fresh basil
